Thanks for the demo last week. We are moving forward with Redwood for inference hosting, but our procurement team hit a couple of gating items when preparing the Coupa enrollment and the MSA/order form. Quick summary: 

- Our legal team has a single MSA with a required signature matrix: for orders > $75k we need a dual-authorized signoff (procurement + finance). We need to understand whether Redwood accepts delegated signatories (i.e., countersignatures by authorized buyers in Coupa) or whether we require an additional manual countersign outside of Coupa.
- Coupa will push vendor-group mapping metadata into the PO payload. We want to confirm the Order Form doesn't prohibit vendor-group level updates and that we can map our internal vendor_group_id to Redwood's vendor record.
- We also require an EDI 997 functional acknowledgment for large volume POs. Can you confirm Redwood's EDI/partner integration supports 997 acks and what the test window would look like?

I attached our internal signer matrix (separately) and the Coupa integration spec for reference. Can your legal and integration teams weigh in today? We're aiming for an onboarding window the week of March 1.

Appreciate any clarity — happy to hop on a short call.

Best,

Hi all — thanks for the clear summary, Lisa. Quick guidance from Legal below and a proposed approach we can take without delaying the Coupa enrollment.

1) Delegated signatories / dual-signature requirement
We can accept electronic signature flows via DocuSign/Equivalents where the signatory has expressly agreed to the MSA terms and the electronic audit trail is retained. To address your dual-signature policy (procurement + finance for >$75k): 
- Option A (preferred): add an Order Form addendum clause that acknowledges a party's internal procurement controls and accepts countersignature via Coupa if Soteria provides a signer matrix tying each authorized Coupa user to a role (procurement / finance) and their authority limits. We will incorporate the signer matrix by reference ("attached as Exhibit A").
- Option B (more conservative): require an additional countersignature outside Coupa (separate DocuSign envelope) for high-value orders.

Proposed redline language (we can include in MSA/Order Form):
"Where Buyer executes an Order via an approved procurement system (e.g., Coupa), Buyer may satisfy signature requirements by designating authorized procurement and finance signatories in a signed Signer Matrix (Exhibit A). Redwood will rely on the Signer Matrix for order execution. For Orders exceeding $75,000, two authorized signatories (procurement and finance) must be recorded in the procurement system and included in Exhibit A. If Buyer cannot provide the Signer Matrix, Buyer must execute a separate countersignature outside the procurement system."

2) Vendor-group mapping in Coupa
We do not have a contractual prohibition on vendor-group metadata. Operationally, we need: vendor_group_id, buyer_vendor_reference, and the vendor's Coupa vendor_id. Kimberley — can your team accept vendor_group mapping on the PO and resolve to an account-level record? If so we should add a short clause that permits Buyer-supplied metadata mapping and describes our fields.

3) EDI 997 functional ack
Mateo — we need an integration confirmation. I suggest we plan an EDI test window (2 business days) and require Soteria's EDI sender/receiver IDs and SFTP endpoint. If we can support 997, we'll confirm by EOD and attach an integration spec.

Attachments: I am attaching a redline of the MSA with the Exhibit A insertion and a draft Order Form flow for e-sign.

Next steps: Camila, propose we offer Option A (accept signers by matrix) and ask Soteria to send the signed Signer Matrix + Coupa vendor metadata. If they prefer Option B, we can accommodate but it will add ~3 business days.

--
Marissa Cole\Senior Counsel, Contracts\Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Coupa onboarding — EDI 997 & partner config

Hi team,

Technical note on EDI 997: Redwood's partner integration layer supports generation and consumption of ANSI X12 997 functional acknowledgements. To proceed I need the following from Soteria:
- EDI sender ID (Soteria) and receiver ID (Redwood) for test and production
- SFTP host, path, and credentials (or API endpoint if you POST EDI payloads)
- Expected interchange control numbers and whether Soteria expects interchange repositioning
- Sample PO payload (Coupa XML is fine) — helps us verify the vendor_group_id field mapping

We typically run a 2-business-day integration test window: Day 1 for connectivity and interchange validation, Day 2 for end-to-end PO->997 verification. If any normalization is required (e.g., vendor_group_id -> internal account_id), that may add one extra day.

Attachments: Integration_Specs_EDI_997.csv (fields we map).

Happy to join a short technical call once Soteria shares IDs.

Thanks — Mateo\Senior Integration Engineer\Redwood Inference
